assembly_steps: Identify all module revisions and match them to the drawings before soldering.
On H2 DevKitM-1 v1.3, remove R7 (470 ohm) with power disconnected; verify USB-UART TX isolation. Use the matched RX23/TX24 RCP image.
Program and verify each loose controller: Nano native USB, H2 native USB Serial/JTAG, and XIAO onboard debug probe with its initial bootloader plus NCP image.
Temporarily wire and test the network update paths before permanently soldering the modules.
Dry-fit physical module and USB bodies, seven mating harness plugs, supports and antenna exclusions. No USB cable corridors are reserved.
Fit seven harness headers and five axial parts. Leave J8 and J9 unpopulated. Solder factory male module pins from underneath; follow physical pad numbers, especially Nano JP2.
Connect the isolated power and external ready modules to the labeled harnesses. Leave local regulator outputs and Nano VBUS isolated from carrier rails.
Check polarity, continuity and loaded rail voltages. Verify Nano VIN/3V3 with concurrent radio traffic.
Commission each service, then test simultaneous operation, network updates, power loss and recovery in the intended enclosure.
manufacturing_claim: One current custom PCB layout; finished vendor modules and external harnesses are still separate physical parts.
unproven: Nano loaded VIN operation below the documented external 6 V minimum
Physical module/connector fit and antenna spacing
H2 R7 isolation, boot straps and network flashing on actual hardware
MG24 bootloader updates and interrupted-transfer recovery on hardware
RF coexistence, range and simultaneous workload reliability
End-to-end ZHA / Thread / Z-Wave commissioning and network backup/restore
